## 1. Supply model

CoinGecko reports a circulating supply of 174M[^mkt.PENDLE.circulating_supply_count] tokens out of a total supply of 282M[^mkt.PENDLE.total_supply_count]. It reports no maximum supply: issuance is either uncapped or the cap is not published.

Circulating market cap is 61.7%[^fund.PENDLE.float_ratio_pct] of fully diluted valuation.

*Requires analyst research.* Issuance or emission schedule and the resulting inflation rate; the unlock calendar (cliff dates and sizes); the initial allocation between team, investors, treasury and community; and any supply sinks other than those DefiLlama counts as holders revenue.

## 2. Utility and demand drivers

Fees are the desk's proxy for demand: what users paid to use the protocol. Over the trailing 365 days[^param.fees_trailing_window_days] users paid $17.3M[^fund.PENDLE.fees_365d_usd]; the last 30 days[^param.runrate_window_days] annualize to $6.60M[^fund.PENDLE.fees_runrate_usd], 0.382x[^fund.PENDLE.fees_runrate_vs_365d_x] the trailing figure, so current usage is running slower than the past year.

DefiLlama fees include payments that go to the supply side (liquidity providers, lenders, stakers or validators), so fees measure activity, not the protocol's earnings.

Trading demand: median daily volume across all venues is $66.4M[^liq.PENDLE.adv_30d_usd] (last reported day: $61.7M[^mkt.PENDLE.volume_24h_usd]).

*Requires analyst research.* What the token is needed for (gas, collateral, staking, governance only, fee discounts); whether using the protocol requires holding or buying the token; who the users are and what alternatives they have.

## 3. Incentive and value-accrual mechanisms

Of the $17.3M[^fund.PENDLE.fees_365d_usd] in trailing fees, the protocol kept $16.9M[^fund.PENDLE.revenue_365d_usd] as revenue (a take rate of 97.8%[^fund.PENDLE.take_rate_365d_pct]).

Most of the fee stream reaches token holders: holders revenue was $13.0M[^fund.PENDLE.holders_revenue_365d_usd] over the trailing year, 75.3%[^fund.PENDLE.holder_share_365d_pct] of fees.

At the pace of the last 30 days[^param.runrate_window_days] it runs at $4.89M[^fund.PENDLE.holders_revenue_runrate_usd] a year, 0.376x[^fund.PENDLE.holders_rev_runrate_vs_365d_x] the trailing figure. Holder cash flow has slowed or stopped recently; the trailing number overstates the current pace.

Valuation multiples (market value divided by the trailing cash flow). Price-to-fees is a usage multiple; price-to-holders-revenue is the closest analogue to a P/E:

| Cash flow | on circulating market cap | on fully diluted valuation |
|---|---|---|
| fees | 25.0x[^fund.PENDLE.p_fees_mcap_x] | 40.5x[^fund.PENDLE.p_fees_fdv_x] |
| revenue | 25.6x[^fund.PENDLE.p_revenue_mcap_x] | 41.4x[^fund.PENDLE.p_revenue_fdv_x] |
| holders revenue | 33.2x[^fund.PENDLE.p_holders_rev_mcap_x] | 53.9x[^fund.PENDLE.p_holders_rev_fdv_x] |

Holders revenue as a yield on circulating market cap: 3.01%[^fund.PENDLE.holder_yield_mcap_pct].

*Requires analyst research.* The mechanism behind holders revenue (buyback, burn, fee switch, staking distribution) and who exactly receives it; whether buybacks are programmatic or discretionary; token emissions paid out as incentives, which are a cost that DefiLlama's fee and revenue series do not net out; treasury size and spending policy.

## 4. Governance

*Requires analyst research.* The desk has no governance data source. To research: who can change fees, emissions and treasury policy (token vote, delegates, a foundation or core team); recent or pending proposals that affect value accrual; admin keys, upgrade powers and timelocks; the legal wrapper and its obligations to token holders.

## 5. Liquidity, market and technical risk

On the consolidated Coinbase + Kraken USD book the spread is 4.04 bps[^liq.PENDLE.spread_bps]. Resting depth is $371,239[^liq.PENDLE.depth_1pct_usd] within ±1%[^param.depth_band_1_pct] of mid and $527,976[^liq.PENDLE.depth_2pct_usd] within ±2%[^param.depth_band_2_pct].

Estimated cost of a market order, worse of buy and sell, half-spread included: 41.8 bps[^liq.PENDLE.slip_100k_bps] for $100,000[^param.order_size_100k_usd]. The visible book could not fill $1M[^param.order_size_1m_usd] or $10M[^param.order_size_10m_usd] within ±15%[^param.book_keep_band_pct] of mid, so no cost is reported for that size: the desk does not extrapolate depth it cannot see.

Volume tells a different story from depth: the median day trades $66.4M[^liq.PENDLE.adv_30d_usd] across all venues (CoinGecko), and Amihud illiquidity is 8.02 bps[^liq.PENDLE.amihud_bps_per_1m] of price move per $1M[^param.order_size_1m_usd] traded. Exiting a $10M[^param.liquidation_position_usd] position at 10%[^param.participation_10_pct] of daily volume takes 1.51 days[^liq.PENDLE.days_to_liq_10m_at_10pct_days]. Reported volume includes venues of uneven quality, so these volume-based figures are optimistic.

Market risk: annualized volatility over the last 90 days[^param.est_window_days] is 77.7%[^risk.PENDLE.vol_90d_ann_pct]. Over the price history the token returned -47.9%[^risk.PENDLE.return_365d_pct] with a maximum drawdown of -79.8%[^risk.PENDLE.max_drawdown_365d_pct]. Correlation of daily returns with BTC is 0.487[^risk.PENDLE.corr_btc_90d].

*Requires analyst research.* Smart-contract and technical risk: audits, exploit history, upgradeability, oracle and bridge dependencies, validator or sequencer concentration; custody support; regulatory status of the token in the jurisdictions that matter to the fund.

## 6. Portfolio context

With positions capped at 10%[^param.max_adv_fraction_pct] of median daily volume, the largest position the desk would hold is $6.64M[^port.PENDLE.max_position_at_cap_usd]. Current target weights: 5%[^port.PENDLE.weight_equal_pct] equal weight, 4.96%[^port.PENDLE.weight_inverse_vol_pct] inverse volatility, 0%[^port.PENDLE.weight_min_var_pct] minimum variance. At its inverse-volatility weight, the cap starts to bind once the fund exceeds $134M[^port.PENDLE.max_aum_before_cap_inverse_vol_usd].

## What the data can't tell us

- **Intent and execution.** Roadmaps, team quality, governance dynamics and competitive threats are outside any of the desk's data sources.
- **The whole market's liquidity.** Depth comes from Coinbase + Kraken only, in one snapshot. Offshore exchanges and on-chain pools usually hold more depth, and depth in a stress event can be a fraction of a calm-day snapshot.
- **Whether DefiLlama's classification is current.** Fee, revenue and holders-revenue labels are DefiLlama's methodology and can lag a governance change. Verify on-chain before relying on them.
- **Causes.** A change in fees or holder revenue is measured, not explained.
- **Execution cost at size.** Larger orders exceed the visible book, and the desk does not extrapolate beyond it.
- **Long-run behaviour.** The desk's long-history price sources (Coin Metrics, and the Binance archive where Coin Metrics has no price) do not cover enough of this token's life, so the memo gives no long-run drawdown or liquidity trend for it.
